successCriteria.description: A `LeaveBalance` entity (canonical name, NOT `Balance`) is exported from `src/modules/balance/balance.model.ts` with the fields id, employeeId, policyId, totalEntitlement, usedDays, remainingDays, fiscalYear, status ('ACTIVE'|'CLOSED'), createdAt, updatedAt.

A `Notification` entity is exported from `src/modules/notification/notification.model.ts` with id, recipientId, type (typed as `NotificationType` imported from `src/shared/types/`), title, message, relatedEntityType, relatedEntityId, status ('PENDING'|'SENT'|'READ'|'ARCHIVED'), createdAt, readAt.

`ILeaveBalanceRepository` and `IBalanceService` interfaces are defined in the balance module, and `INotificationRepository` and `INotificationService` interfaces are defined in the notification module.
`PgLeaveBalanceRepository` implements `ILeaveBalanceRepository` and maps camelCase fields to snake_case columns employee_id, policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year.
`PgNotificationRepository` implements `INotificationRepository` and maps camelCase fields to snake_case columns recipient_id, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, read_at.

Each module's `index.ts` barrel exports its model, interfaces, and repository (balance: `balance.model.ts` + `balance.repository.ts`; notification: `notification.model.ts` + `notification.repository.ts`).

The balance arithmetic rule is encoded in the model/interface: `availableDays = entitlementDays - usedDays - pendingDays` is DERIVED (never a stored field) and MAY go negative (no clamping); the three stored counters (totalEntitlement, usedDays, remainingDays) are NON-NEGATIVE and a transition taking usedDays/pendingDays below zero is an ERROR.

constraints: Do NOT build services, routes, or tests in this phase — only models, interfaces, repositories, and index barrels. Service interfaces (IBalanceService, INotificationService) are declared but not implemented.

All database access goes through the repository layer only (GP-001); repositories use the shared `pool` from `src/shared/db/connection.ts` and never import a pool/client/module-level db helper elsewhere.
Repository methods that may join a caller's transaction take the client as an optional LAST parameter and fall back to the shared pool when omitted (AGENTS.md Architecture rules 5).
TypeScript identifiers are camelCase; database columns are snake_case; the repository is the ONLY layer that maps between them. No snake_case in TS field names, no camelCase in SQL.
Use `unknown` with type guards instead of `any` (HARNESS constraint `no-any`).
Modules import from each other ONLY through their public `index.ts` entry point; no circular dependencies.
outOfScope: Service implementations (BalanceService, NotificationService) — deferred to Phase 6 (part 2/2).
Route files and HTTP endpoints for balance and notification — deferred to Phase 6.
Unit tests for balance/notification — deferred to Phase 6 (tests/unit/modules/balance/balance.service.spec.ts, tests/unit/modules/notification/notification.service.spec.ts).
DB migrations / schema DDL for leave_balances and notifications tables — not part of this phase's file scope.

ambiguities.description: The balance arithmetic rule references `pendingDays`, but the LeaveBalance entity field list has no `pendingDays` field (only totalEntitlement, usedDays, remainingDays). Is `pendingDays` a separate stored counter to be added, or is it derived from leave requests in the leave module (Phase 7) and thus not a field on LeaveBalance in this phase?
options: pendingDays is NOT a LeaveBalance field in this phase — it is supplied by the leave module at approval time; the derived formula is documented in the model/interface but only totalEntitlement/usedDays/remainingDays are stored
Add a pendingDays field to LeaveBalance now (diverging from the reconciled entity shape)
pendingDays is derived from remainingDays vs usedDays internally

ambiguities.description: The phase says "the three stored counters are NON-NEGATIVE" but the entity has totalEntitlement, usedDays, remainingDays — and the rule separately names usedDays/pendingDays. Which exact fields are the "three stored counters" that must be non-negative?
options: totalEntitlement, usedDays, remainingDays (the three fields on the entity)
usedDays, pendingDays, remainingDays (per the arithmetic rule text)

ambiguities.description: The reconciled dependency map says balance depends on audit, but this phase's file scope (models + interfaces + repositories only) does not require an audit import. Should the balance repository/service interface reference audit now, or is that dependency realized only in Phase 6 when the service writes audit records?
options: No audit reference in this phase; the dependency is realized in Phase 6 (service layer)
Declare the audit dependency in IBalanceService now (e.g. an audit method signature) even though it is not implemented

entityInvariants.invariant: `availableDays = entitlementDays - usedDays - pendingDays` is DERIVED and never stored; it MAY go negative (no clamping). The three stored counters (totalEntitlement, usedDays, remainingDays) are NON-NEGATIVE; a transition taking usedDays/pendingDays below zero is an ERROR, not a clamp.
Lifecycle status is restricted to 'PENDING' | 'SENT' | 'READ' | 'ARCHIVED'; `readAt` is set only when the notification transitions to READ.
`type` is typed as the shared `NotificationType` enum (imported from `src/shared/types/`), not a free-form string.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Persists a LeaveBalance row and returns the persisted entity; rejects a non-negative-counter violation (usedDays/remainingDays/totalEntitlement below zero) with a typed error rather than clamping.
A transition that would take usedDays or pendingDays below zero is an ERROR (typed error), never a clamp; the derived availableDays is never written.
Persists a Notification row and returns the persisted entity; `type` must be a valid NotificationType value.
Sets status to READ and stamps readAt; an illegal transition (e.g. from ARCHIVED) is rejected with a typed error.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Import `NotificationType` from `src/shared/types/index.ts` (re-exported from `notification-type.ts`) for the Notification.type field — do not redefine it locally.

Repository methods that join a caller's transaction take the client as an optional LAST parameter and fall back to the shared `pool` when omitted — matching the pattern established by `PgAuditLogRepository`.
Repositories obtain the shared pool from `src/shared/db/connection.ts` (exports `pool`) and never import a pool/client/module-level db helper elsewhere.

The `IUnitOfWork` contract (`withTransaction<T>(fn: (client: PoolClient) => Promise<T>)`) is the only transaction boundary; repositories do NOT own `withTransaction` and do NOT issue BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK.
Barrel export style matches the existing modules: `export { X } from './file'` / `export type { ... } from './file'`.

LeaveBalance field names/types match the reconciled entity shape (id, employeeId, policyId, totalEntitlement, usedDays, remainingDays, fiscalYear, status, createdAt, updatedAt) and the canonical name `LeaveBalance` (not `Balance`).

integrationPoints.why: Notification.type is typed as the shared NotificationType enum; balance/notification may also reference shared DTOs (BalanceSnapshot) and countLeaveDays.
Repositories obtain the shared pg Pool for all SQL access.
Participating repository methods accept an optional PoolClient (last param) to join a caller's transaction; the IUnitOfWork contract governs the boundary.
Balance mutations will later write audit records (GP-002); the balance module depends on audit per the reconciled dependency map.
